findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed ice and cut fruit to be in bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sink is being used solely for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed bar dish machine to test at 0ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, the dish machine was primed and was observed to test at 100 ppm. Ensure sanitizing dish machines are testing at 100ppm to ensure dishes are being properly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past 7 date marking maximum. Items included pie, noodles, sauces, and deli meats. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item held longer than 7 days is discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed current CFM to not have allergen training completed. Discussed with PIC, allergen training will be completed. Ensure the required allergen training is completed by all CFM’s. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed a member staff to not use a barrier when turning off hand sink after washing hands. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing. Ensure staff is properly washing. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the sanitizer dispensing unit to not be dispensing sanitizer. The sanitizer bucket pulled from the unit also tested at 0 ppm Quat. Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer was not plugged into dispenser. The sanitizer would not stay plugged in so a work order has been placed, yet it was still able to provided the correct amount of concentration when manually held in place.  Service will be called for and the inspector will conduct a follow up inspection. Ensure facility has sanitizer available and at the correct concentration at all hours of operation. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.comment:

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Inspector observed priority and priority foundation items during the inspection today. Ensure that person in charge is actively aware of what constitutes Priority and Priority foundation items and takes measures to avoid these violations whenever possible. PIC was coached on temperature logs for the cold holding units, using test strips daily for the chemical sanitizer dispenser in the facility. The violation is considered corrected on site.  

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee place their bare hand on lettuce in an attempt to determine the lettuce temperature. Bare hand contact with ready to eat food is not allowed. Refrain from touching foods that no longer need to be washed or cooked with bare hands. The employee was coached immediately and the lettuce was then discarded in the garbage. The violation is considered corrected on site.  

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.comment:

Ensure that this food contact equipment is cleaned and sanitized before the follow up inspection on 5/14/24. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed three cold holding units where food was being held out of temperature:
1) The cooler across from the grill area has a bottom left drawer holding 3 bs of ribs at 45.5F and 3 lbs of Philly meat at 47.2F. These meats were discarded in the garbage. Other items in the cooler top left drawer (ham 39), right side upper and lower drawers are holding various cheeses between 38F and 40F. Service will be called to ensure that the unit is functioning properly. Use unit properly as well. Do not put hot foods in the unit to cool (plastic wrap on ribs had condensation drops on it) and keep unit pulled out away from the wall so that air flow is not restricted.  Thermometer in the unit read 38F
2) The cooler on the left at salad (with drawers) is holding cut fruit with melon at 47F, a single bottle of house made salad dressing at 46F, and lettuce at 47F and 49F. These items were discarded in the garbage. Use cooler properly by keeping the top filled with pans or lids at all times. Lettuce in the left side top drawer of this unit was in a tightly closed bag in a pan. The lettuce on the right was in a pan that is too big to properly fit in the unit. The cut fruit was in a mixing bowl that was in a pan. Do not double pan food items that are placed in prep cooler for cold holding. Thermometer in the unit reads 42F. The unit will be evaluated. Other items in the top of the unit are between 38 and 41F. Keep an eye on this unit today. The internal thermometer has raised from 42F to 45F.  Temperature of food in the top of the make table has raised to 44F. The unit is no longer going to be used. Items from the top of the unit were moved to the walk in. 
3) The make table in the snack bar has 4 cups of pre packaged guacamole labeled keep refrigerated at 45F. The independent thermometer in the unit reads 41F. The cups of guacamole were discarded. The snack bar will not open until labor day. All snack bar equipment will be cleaned and evaluated before being put into use. 
Food temperature violations are considered corrected on site. Ensure that units are working and being used properly for food safety. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a house made dressing in a squeeze bottle in the top of the salad make table on the left. The contents of the bottle were 46F. The dressing was not labeled with a date marking. The bottle was in a pan in the top of the unit. The contents of the bottle were discarded. Take care not to double pan items in make tables. Mark all TCS ready to eat foods with 7 day date markings. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Inspector observed whisks in the kitchen stored in a container with their handles down and food contact surfaces up so that they had to be touched in order to remove the whisks from the container. Store food equipment properly protected. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed boxes of single use cups on the floor in the dry storage area of the basement. There is also a stack of paper boats in the dry storage stored with food contact surfaces up and exposed to dust and soil. Store all clean articles properly protected. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a baking mat with slices through it and a spatula with cracks and a gouge. These items were discarded as they are not longer smooth or easily cleanable. Take note of equipment condition and discard when it is no longer in compliance with this section. 

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the snack bar kitchen to have accumulated and encrusted soil in the oven, low boy drawers, under the grills on the low boy, in the prep top lid of the make table. The facility was closed in the fall and the facility has not been used since that time according to the staff. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The facility has a vent to the right of the opening to the chef’s office. The vent has an accumulation of dust. The vent is a draw and therefore collects dust and dirt. The exit light also has an accumulation of dust on it. Clean this area and maintain it clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
